implication: Reinforces external runtime mediation and audit requirements for multi-agent interactions rather than treating agent safety as static prompt filters or single-model alignment.

title: The AI Evaluation Ecosystem
summary: Dave et al. model the interactions among model developers, evaluators, and users using generative agent simulations to study benchmark design. They find private holdout benchmarks reduce the gap between benchmark rankings and actual user satisfaction compared to public test sets.
implication: Demonstrates that public evaluation datasets suffer from gaming and saturation, reinforcing the need for continuous holdout evaluation in measuring agent capabilities.

title: Strategic Governance of AI Models in Earth Science
summary: Kelp et al. identify systemic shortcomings in relying exclusively on benchmark skill metrics to evaluate foundation models in Earth science. They propose open physics-based evaluation standards and dedicated safety research to decouple nominal test accuracy from operational reliability.
implication: Highlights the distinction between nominal benchmark skill and real-world reliability under non-stationary conditions, supporting rigorous independent observational criteria.

title: A Trust Layer for Agent Evaluation
summary: Researchers propose a post-hoc verification layer for agent benchmarks that checks whether scores were earned via traceable computation and hold under repeated runs, finding that only 22.6% of recorded passes withstand verification.
implication: Supports independent verification and trace audits over unverified benchmark pass claims for autonomous systems.

title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
summary: A test-time failure recovery architecture retrieves conditional failure lessons on demand without cluttering the agent's context, improving recovery rates across benchmarks by 37% over runtime intervention baselines.
implication: Demonstrates that modular external monitors and targeted recovery advice yield higher agent reliability than stuffing agent contexts with exhaustive rules.

title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
summary: Mingbird demonstrates that small open-weight models running on local laptops fail primarily due to cloud-scale harnesses rather than model weights. A local-first harness with net-zero prefill and finish gates dramatically improves reliability.
implication: Validates local execution of personal agents on modest hardware, showing that harness architecture and deterministic completion guards make local models viable without relying on cloud providers.

title: Agentao: A Policy-Governed Runtime Harness for Embeddable Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: Agentao introduces a local-first embeddable runtime architecture that decouples agent tool proposals from host-authorized execution, enforcing explicit boundaries, policy gates, and structured traces.
implication: Reinforces the default-deny agent runtime pattern where host policies gate all tool side effects and maintain structured audit traces rather than allowing unconstrained tool execution.

title: AgentSociety 2: An Integrated Research Environment for Executable Social Science
summary: Introduces AgentSociety 2, an integrated research environment coupling AI social scientists and silicon participants in a single runtime to execute end-to-end computational social experiments.
implication: Sandboxed simulations of agent governance can couple experiment-orchestrating agents with participant agents within the same deterministic runtime.

title: TRACER: Trajectory-Aligned Learning for Multi-Turn User Simulation
summary: Presents TRACER, a multi-turn user simulator combining supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with hierarchical rewards to model evolving user intent and match real conversational trajectories.
implication: Simulations evaluating agent communication and clarifying questions should align multi-turn user simulators against empirical interaction distributions rather than naive roleplaying.

title: AgenTEE: Confidential LLM Agent Execution on Edge Devices
summary: Researchers introduce AgenTEE, which uses hardware-isolated confidential virtual machines to run language model agent runtimes, inference engines, and tools on edge devices with under 5.15% overhead.
implication: Demonstrates hardware-enforced isolation for personal agent runtimes on user devices without trusting host hypervisors, confirming the feasibility of private local agent containment.

title: Explainer for the Prompt API
source: W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group
summary: The W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group proposes a standardized browser Prompt API allowing web apps to access built-in on-device models for private local processing and offline execution.
implication: Browser-native model execution standards enable client-side personal AI interfaces to run locally without exposing raw personal prompts to remote services.

title: Spatial Pattern Formation from Multi-Agent Learning in Public Goods Dilemmas
summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning in spatial public goods games reveals that cooperator learning creates clusters around resource peaks, reducing collective welfare below random movement due to crowding unless externality costs are charged.
implication: In multi-agent economies, uncoordinated individual learning causes crowding and welfare losses that require transparent feedback on human and resource costs to resolve.

title: The Orchestration of Multi-Agent Systems: Architectures, Protocols, and Enterprise Adoption
summary: A technical framework formalizing multi-agent orchestration architectures, contrasting the Model Context Protocol for tool integration with the Agent2Agent protocol for peer coordination, negotiation, and policy-compliant delegation.
implication: Validates the separation between tool-use protocols and peer-to-peer agent coordination layers, reinforcing modular agent runtime designs.

title: Cited but Not Consulted: A Counterfactual Audit of Legal Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
summary: A counterfactual audit shows language models frequently cite legal authorities without their verdicts depending on them. Swapping governing statutes leaves decisions unchanged in most tests, proving that generated reasoning is often unfaithful.
implication: Auditing systems cannot trust model-generated chain-of-thought explanations as evidence of compliance. Transparent deterministic checks and independent observers are required.

title: Beyond Single-Model Injection: A Threat Model and Defense Architecture for Prompt Injection in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: A multi-agent prompt injection threat model of 14 vectors showing 67% vulnerability in a 6-agent system, mitigated to 4.2% via message signing, boundary sanitization, and scoped tool access.
implication: Confirms that prompt-level guardrails fail across agent boundaries; inter-agent messaging and tool invocations require cryptographic signing and strict per-role capability scopes.

title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape
summary: An open benchmark (SANDBOXESCAPEBENCH) testing LLM container breakout capabilities across configuration errors, privilege mistakes, kernel flaws, and runtime weaknesses.
implication: Demonstrates that container-only sandboxing without hardware virtualization or microVM isolation is vulnerable to automated exploit discovery by frontier models.

title: You can contribute if you... An Empirical Framework of AI Contribution Policies in OSS
summary: Empirical study analyzing open source policies on AI contributions, showing communities regulate AI submissions to protect maintainer attention, enforce accountability, and maintain newcomer pathways.
implication: Shows that value recognition systems cannot treat raw AI output and human labor identically without overwhelming maintainers and eroding authentic credit.

title: The AI Layoff Trap
summary: Theoretical model demonstrating that competitive firms over-automate because individual cost savings exceed private demand loss, creating an arms race that universal basic income alone cannot fix.
implication: Shows why replacing fiat wages requires multi-dimensional value feedback and collective coordination rather than post-hoc monetary redistribution alone.

title: Fairness in Token Delegation: Mitigating Voting Power Concentration in DAOs
summary: Empirical study across 14 DAO forums shows delegation rankings reinforce extreme voting power concentration (Gini > 0.94) and misalign delegates from token holder priorities.
implication: Confirms that naive token delegation reproduces corporate oligarchies; CIN's multi-dimensional value feedback and plural governance must avoid simple ranking-based delegation interfaces.

title: Loop-Back Authority in LLM Agent Teams: A Paired Experiment on Flat and Hierarchical Coordination
summary: In a paired experiment across 86 runs, flat LLM teams outperformed hierarchical teams with manager loop-back authority in utility and clarity, with supervisory revision degrading quality and adding 51.5% token overhead.
implication: Supports CIN's goal of peer coordination over manager hierarchy in agent runtime design: supervisors without objective verification mechanisms degrade outputs.

title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
summary: Introduces AI-Work to simulate LLM agents in a gig economy without wage floors, finding that agents with metacognition, competitive awareness, and long-horizon planning capture market share while unconstrained competition drives down prices.
implication: Unregulated agent labor markets rapidly commodify cognitive tasks; personal twins need explicit wage floors, reputation verification, and human-in-the-loop approval to protect human livelihoods.

title: How Well Does Agent Development Reflect Real-World Work?
summary: Audits 43 agent benchmarks and 72,342 tasks across 1,016 US occupations, finding that agent evaluation is heavily programming-centric and largely ignores the broader categories where human labor and economic value are concentrated.
implication: Benchmarking twins solely on coding leaves non-programming human labor unrepresented; twin labor designs must model diverse occupations and granular human approval boundaries.

title: Interpretability as Alignment: Making Internal Understanding a Design Principle
summary: Frames mechanistic interpretability as a core architectural design constraint and audit substrate for verifiable causal alignment, moving beyond post-hoc explanations to enable robust assurance pipelines.
implication: Directly grounds our research agenda on model verification and independent watchers in causal abstraction substrates for private assurance and auditability.

title: A First Look At Efficient And Secure On-Device LLM Inference Against KV Leakage
summary: Demonstrates that on-device GPU LLM inference leaks key-value cache states that can reconstruct conversations, and proposes TEE-based weight permutations to prevent leakage.
implication: Personal on-device agents running on untrusted local accelerators need memory isolation or permutation to keep conversation geometry confidential.
